video_title: Can The Clippers Ever Recover?! | Rachel Nichols and Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: LA Clippers punished by NBA for year-long investigation
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers last week were punished severely by the NBA in the aftermath of the results being revealed.
quotes.quote: The Clippers last week were punished severely by the NBA in the aftermath of the results being revealed of this year-long investigation. Five first-round picks docked from the LA Clippers. Steve Ballmer, the owner, he gets suspended for a year. Gillian Zucker, she gets suspended for a year. Lawrence Frank, he gets suspended for six months, $30 million fine for the LA Clippers.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Reporters felt deceived by the Clippers during investigation
quotes.excerpt: I've heard from a lot of reporters who have expressed real frustration at what they were told.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I've heard from a lot of reporters who have expressed real frustration at what they were told by the Clippers. They feel deceived by the Clippers. I was too far gone, I was pretty close-minded on this from jump, because to me, my thought was, if it looks like a duck and it walks like a duck, it's probably a duck.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I just said, hey, we got to wait and see what the investigation happens, right?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols on the betrayal of long-term NBA relationships
quotes.excerpt: It's a bummer to have people you've known for 20, 25 years who looked you in the eye.
quotes.quote: It's a bummer to have people you've known for 20, 25 years who looked you in the eye and lied to your face. Because I want everyone out there to think about people they've known for 25 years. If that person looked at you and said, hey man, this just isn't what you think it is, wait for the investigation, you'd be like, all right, I'm at least going to give them the benefit of the doubt. I never did that, and I don't think a lot of people ever did that. The benefit of the doubt was, well, let's wait and see. Let's see what people who, in Pablo Torre's words, with more subpoena power than I have, can find out.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Questions about Clippers leadership and future direction
quotes.excerpt: Who's running the organization right now? I don't know. Where are they going to go?
quotes.quote: Who's running the organization right now? I don't know. Where are they going to go in terms of direction of the team? You brought up last week, does Ballmer sell the team? There are some really, really, really big picture questions here beyond the nuts and bolts of sort of how do they manage draft picks for the next couple years.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Trent Redden expected to lead Clippers basketball operations
quotes.excerpt: We all assume that Trent Redden, who didn't get touched by this report, is going to take over.
quotes.quote: We all assume that Trent Redden, who didn't get touched by this report, is going to take over as head of basketball operations. But again, there's a reason why you have a full basketball unit there, and so now you have the leader is gone. So Trent becomes a leader, and then what? Like what happens under him? Who makes the decision if they want to hire more people in the basketball office? Like who's making the decision on the business operation side, which is not a small job?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Uncertainty surrounding Ty Lue's future with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: Do you talk to Ty Lue at some point? Like Ty, do you want to be here?
quotes.quote: Do you talk to Ty Lue at some point? Like Ty, do you want to be here? Like do you want to be part of what's going to be a decade-long rebuild? I mean, I think he's got three years left on his contract. Do you want to be part of that?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' future hampered by loss of first-round picks
quotes.excerpt: They lose their next five first-round draft picks, that not only mitigates their ability to get good young players.
quotes.quote: They lose their next five first-round draft picks, that not only mitigates their ability to get good young players, it almost destroys their ability to make a trade of any kind of particular meaning. You want to close this deal for Kawhi Leonard because you want to try to get those two first-round picks, the swap. You want to start to rebuild some of that draft capital, but beyond that, how do you see the Clippers operating in the foreseeable future?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Lack of long-term planning in the Clippers front office
quotes.excerpt: I just don't know how much long-term planning is done by who right now.
quotes.quote: I just don't know how much long-term planning is done by who right now. Are you planning for the next two years? You planning for the next five years? You planning for the next seven years? I think you just trying to basically bottom out. You don't control your picks, you don't benefit from being bad the way some of these teams that have been tanking over the last three or four years do, because other people have your picks or your picks don't exist anymore.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Toronto Raptors expected to honor the Clippers trade agreement
quotes.excerpt: I have heard only that Toronto is going to honor the deal as constructed.
quotes.quote: I have heard only that Toronto is going to honor the deal as constructed. I haven't heard anything else, but they certainly don't have to. And it would be interesting to see whether they, this hasn't gone as of you and I sitting here, this hasn't gone through yet. It would be interesting to see if there's been any pick up in conversation of, well, actually we'd like this, or how about this, or one less of that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors' animosity toward Clippers over previous trade dealings
quotes.excerpt: The Raptors, they hate the Clippers. Like they hate them. It's the same front office.
quotes.quote: The Raptors, they hate the Clippers. Like they hate them. It's the same front office, yes, over this player and how these decisions set them back. I don't know if they were ever really in the mix to resign Kawhi Leonard back in those days. Was he going to go to LA always, Lakers or Clippers? Probably, but they had meetings and they were, yeah, the Clippers clearly broke the rules to get him, to keep him.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA culture of keeping one's word in trade deals
quotes.excerpt: There is this ethos in the NBA of you got to stick to your word.
quotes.quote: There is this ethos in the NBA of you got to stick to your word, people aren't going to want to do deals with you in the future if you don't. First of all, I think people in the NBA do deals with who's convenient for them to do deals with. Dan Gilbert wrote that terrible Comic Sans letter to LeBron and still worked with him and Rich Paul to do a sign and trade to Miami. Like that all happened. It's not like he went to Miami as a free agent, it was actually a sign and trade when Cleveland sent him to Miami the first time.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers must act as a receptacle for bad contracts
quotes.excerpt: They've got to act like the Wizards have acted, like the Thunder have acted, like the Nets.
quotes.quote: They've got to act like the Wizards have acted, like the Thunder have acted, like the Nets have acted. You have got to be a receptacle for bad contracts in order to get a draft pick back in return. If some team's out there and says, oh god, we've got to get this guy off our books, we'll sweeten the offer with a first-round pick, that's who the Clippers are for at least the next five years. You're not going to win, you're not going to be able to attract top talent, you're not going to be able to make trades. What you can do is start to rebuild that draft capital through these types of transactions.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' draft pick situation compared to Clippers
quotes.excerpt: The most recent case that kind of compares to this a little bit is the Timberwolves.
quotes.quote: The most recent case that kind of compares to this a little bit is the Timberwolves, the Joe Smith. There actually was an email that says, we are going to do this for X, right? That was during the David Stern era, five first-round draft picks, and then slowly over time, they got one back, then they got, you know, another one back a year and a half later. That was a different time. That was not when the internet was going crazy the way it is. It was not when there are as many talk shows as there are right now.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's decision to pass on contract extension
quotes.excerpt: Nikola Jokic electing not to sign a contract extension this summer.
quotes.quote: Nikola Jokic electing not to sign a contract extension this summer, this is the second year in a row he has passed on an extension. The thinking is that financially, it's much better for Jokic to go into free agency next summer. He can sign a five-year, $360 million deal, the richest deal in NBA history. So financially, it makes all the sense in the world, but it does make for, I think, a lot of unease in Denver, within the organization, within the fan base, that crazy stuff can happen.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Jokic's love for Europe vs. LeBron's love for North America
quotes.excerpt: I love how you're like, Jokic loves Europe. That's like LeBron loves North America.
quotes.quote: I love how you're like, Jokic loves Europe. That's like LeBron loves North America. Like Europe's a continent, man. But he likes going home is what I'm saying. He likes going home. Likes to race his horses, likes to live his life. And look, he's accomplished all he needs to accomplish. Like he's an NBA champion, he is a multi-time MVP, he's a multi-multi-multi-time All-Star, like nothing left to prove in the NBA on a basketball level.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Misconception about Jokic's competitiveness
quotes.excerpt: I think it is a huge misconception around basketball that Nikola Jokic is not interested.
quotes.quote: I think it is a huge misconception around basketball that Nikola Jokic is not interested in winning championships and is not competitive. He is absolutely interested in winning NBA titles and is competitive because he could not play at the level he is with the dedication it requires unless he was. So that's the first thing. I think he wants to stay around and I think he wants to win again.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' roster depth issues after offseason moves
quotes.excerpt: This offseason, the Nuggets got worse. They lose Peyton Watson and that sign and trade deal.
quotes.quote: This offseason, the Nuggets got worse. They lose Peyton Watson and that sign and trade deal, they lose Tim Hardaway Jr., good player off the bench for them. They add DeMar DeRozan, good player still, back end of his career. Spencer Dinwiddie is back, Julian Strawther is still there, Jonas Valanciunas is gone. They still have one of the best starting lineups in the NBA, but they have consistently had one of the best starting lineups in the NBA. Their problem in the last couple of years has been a lack of depth and they continue to hemorrhage talent.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' failure to pay Tim Connelly
quotes.excerpt: How much money do you think they didn't want to pay Tim Connelly after that title?
quotes.quote: How much money do you think they didn't want to pay Tim Connelly after that title, and that he went to Minnesota, and the success he's had working his absolute magic for the Timberwolves? How much money have they ended up having to spend in luxury tax and just losing out on money in playoff rounds and playoff money and possibly another title and things like that?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' lack of depth is a major concern
quotes.excerpt: They don't have a good backup to Jokic right now. Marvin Bagley is the backup on paper.
quotes.quote: They don't have a good backup to Jokic right now. Marvin Bagley is the backup on paper. No offense to Marvin Bagley, but I think Jonas Valanciunas is better than him. So I'm curious what happens in that month to two months before the trade deadline and sort of teams start to figure out who they are and who they aren't and players we don't think of are available right now, become available.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's impact on the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: I think Donovan Mitchell is a phenomenal player. But when I think it's an unfair question.
quotes.quote: I think Donovan Mitchell is a phenomenal player. But when I think it's an unfair question a little bit when we say, oh, can he be the best player on a championship team, only in that like who's around him is so important. Jalen Brunson is a champion in every way we talk about champions, right? Heart of a champion, will of a champion, leadership of a champion, and so skilled, right? And able to come through in the clutch in so many ways both, you know, actually on the court but then also for his team.
